assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase is the enzyme behind biological N2 fixation. Structures of the Fe protein, the MoFe protein and the FeMo-cofactor, together with kinetic work on the electron-transfer and ATP-gated cycle, give a physical-mechanistic account of a chemically very hard reaction. This is the kind of mechanism in a living system that I weight most heavily.
assessment.attribution: Credit divides among structural work (Rees, Einsle and the Dean/Rees/Ribbe lineage), cofactor biosynthesis (Ribbe, Dean) and mechanism and kinetics (Seefeldt, Dean). Three names cannot cover all of it. Rees and Einsle represent the structural decisions, including the central carbide, and Seefeldt represents the mechanistic and kinetic side.
assessment.maturity: Structures go back decades and have been repeatedly confirmed, including recent cryo-EM of turnover states. The mechanism of N2 binding and reduction is still under active debate, so the field is mature but its mechanistic core is not closed.
uncertainties: The identity and sequence of intermediates in N2 reduction is unsettled.
Dean, Ribbe and others have strong claims, so the three-name limit forces a contestable cut.
I am relying on my own recollection of the structural history rather than verified evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is a unifying physical concept for how electrons and protons move together in enzymes, including respiratory and photosynthetic enzymes, and in molecular electrocatalysis. Its theoretical framework and its experimental demonstrations underpin the energy-conversion mechanisms I work on.
assessment.attribution: Meyer (early PCET and the concerted-pathway concept), Mayer (bond-weakening thermochemistry, concerted proton-electron transfer), Nocera (model systems, solar fuels) and Hammes-Schiffer (theory) made distinct contributions. Meyer's priority is strong, but a fair three-person configuration is arguable and I would weigh the committee's view on priority carefully.
assessment.maturity: The concept is well established and widely used across chemistry and biochemistry. Recognition would be timely, although it risks reading as a recognition of a conceptual field rather than one discovery.
uncertainties: Priority among Meyer, Mayer and Nocera is not clean.
Whether the prize would be for the concept or for a specific discovery is unclear.
The Meyer omission would need to be justified; I proposed three names without Meyer for balance but this is a real choice.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-range electron transfer through proteins explains how redox proteins exchange electrons over large distances, through tunnelling pathways and a quantitative distance dependence. Time-resolved spectroscopy on modified proteins made the physics measurable. This is close to my own field and is a clear case of mechanism backed by kinetics.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler are the clear core, with a long and consistent body of work on ruthenium-modified proteins. Other contributors in the electron-transfer theory (Marcus, already recognized; Beratan, Onuchic) are not in the credited set, so the supplied credit supports a clean two-person prize.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation and wide uptake in bioenergetics, though it is an older and incremental line without a single recent breakthrough, so timing is neither premature nor urgent.
uncertainties: The work may read as an elaboration of the Marcus theory prize rather than as a new discovery.
The committee may judge that the impact outside bioinorganic chemistry is limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensation and liquid-liquid phase separation reframed intracellular organization, and bring physical chemistry (phase diagrams, multivalency) into cell biology. The shift in thinking is large and broad.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne made the foundational P-granule observations. Rosen supplied the quantitative multivalent-interaction framework. Pappu and Mittag are also important for the sequence-grammar side. The core trio is reasonably defensible.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly growing and influential, but many functional claims remain contested, including in-vivo physiological relevance of phase separation versus other assemblies. Possibly early.
uncertainties: Physiological significance and the right physical description remain debated.
Whether this is chemistry or cell biology for the purposes of the chemistry prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by induced proximity, via PROTACs and molecular glues, introduced a new chemical modality that is now in clinical development. The mechanistic chemistry of ternary-complex formation is elegant.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies defined the original PROTAC concept. Ciulli made the structure-guided, VHL-based design that made it practical. The molecular-glue branch (Handa, Ito, Gray) is separate and may need different recognition, which complicates a single prize.
assessment.maturity: Strong clinical momentum, with first approvals still pending, so the full medical impact is not yet visible. The mechanistic literature is large and consistent.
uncertainties: Compound discovery: PROTACs and molecular glues are different stories.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography with X-ray free-electron lasers permits structures before radiation damage and time-resolved structural movies of reactions in enzymes and photoreceptors. It is a method that makes dynamic mechanisms visible, which I value highly.
assessment.attribution: Chapman, Fromme, Schlichting and Hajdu all made decisive contributions to the early demonstrations and to the time-resolved applications. Hajdu's early role is a priority question, and three names cannot cover the group.
assessment.maturity: Methods are established, with several confirmed time-resolved biological applications, although the technique's reach is limited by facility access.
uncertainties: Attribution among Hajdu, Chapman, Fromme and Schlichting is uncertain.
Number of landmark biochemical discoveries produced is still modest compared with the method's promise.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional NMR methods for large biomolecules and for dynamics (relaxation, TROSY, relaxation dispersion) opened solution studies of proteins, including sparsely populated states, in a way no other method does.
assessment.attribution: Kay, Bax and Clore are the most plausible decisive contributors; Palmer and Wagner are also credited, so the three-laureate cap excludes people with real claims. Wüthrich's 2002 prize overlaps the field, which complicates the novelty argument.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely adopted and extensively confirmed.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier NMR prizes may reduce perceived novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base to another without double-strand breaks, by combining deaminase chemistry with a programmable CRISPR scaffold. It is a clear chemical-biology invention with direct therapeutic relevance.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the central figure. Komor and Gaudelli were the lead authors of the cytosine and adenine base editors. Nishida and Kondo have a parallel claim for the deaminase-Cas9 fusion, but a Liu-centred prize is the cleanest.
assessment.maturity: Clinical use is emerging, and the Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2020 already recognized CRISPR, so this would need a clear separation from that award.
uncertainties: Whether a prime-editing candidacy (B028) should be combined with it.
